newsitem.title: GERMANY: German CDU readies tax reform proposal.
newsitem.headline: German CDU readies tax reform proposal.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) on Tuesday set down their proposals for a sweeping tax reform that would cut Germany's top income tax rate to about 35 percent from the current 53 percent.
The party's plan is broadly in line with an outline put forward on Monday by Finance Minister Theo Waigel, who said he saw the top rate falling to between 35 and 40 percent.
The CDU will present the plan at a party congress at the end of the month. Waigel's tax reform commission has until the end of the year to make its final proposal.
The three-page CDU paper said the tax reform was aimed at cutting taxpayers' burden substantially, but it did not specify a figure.

On Monday, Waigel said his plan would result in 20 billion to 30 billion marks in net relief for taxpayers, on gross reductions of 80 billion to 90 billion marks. The difference is the result of tighter rules on deductions and a broadening of the tax base, Waigel said.
The CDU plan would cut the minimum income tax rate to less than 20 percent from the current 26 percent.
